problems.issue: The closing sentence of the note says prototype/app/data/sentences.json carries the same romaji. It does not. prototype/scripts/sync-data.mjs builds that file's romaji with spacedRomaji(), which joins the per-token romaji with spaces and falls back to the bank's glued romaji field only when a record has no tokens. A grep for each of the five defective sentence strings finds them in corpus/sentences/bank.json and in historical fable5_validation audit files, never in the prototype export. The consequence is only descriptive: the 11 token fixes do propagate to the prototype on a re-sync, the 5 sentence-level romaji fixes do not reach it at all, and the instruction to re-run the exporter is still correct and still needed.

Two encoding defects on the single needs-human row. Its fix is the empty string where every other non-fix row in the queue carries null, which contradicts the queue's own stated contract and is a mechanical-apply hazard: an applier keyed on fix being non-null would write an empty string into an integer field. Its current is the string 71 while the stored value is the integer 71, so this one anchor is not literally byte-exact. The substance of the row is sound and independently confirmed: the token reads はいれる while vocab 71 is kanji 入 kana いれる, a different lexeme, and the godan-potential-null habit the row cites is real across the bank.

The why calls the dropped って the quoting particle. In this sentence it is the colloquial topic marker, which the record's own structure_explanation states in pt-BR as a spoken form of は or というのは introducing the subject. The label is wrong only in the rationale; the observation that って is missing from the stored romaji is correct and the fix value is unaffected, since the token stores tte either way.
